gloss: game record (shogi, go, chess); score sheet of a board game

definitions.gloss: game record (of shogi, go, or chess); notation of moves
definitions.explanation: A written or digital record of the moves played in a game of shogi, go, or (less often) chess. Kept for later study and analysis, and a central part of how professional and amateur players learn. Published for major professional matches in magazines, newspapers, and online databases.

examples.japanese: プロの{棋譜|きふ}を{並|なら}べて{勉強|べんきょう}する。
examples.english: I study by playing through professional game records.

examples.japanese: {名人戦|めいじんせん}の{棋譜|きふ}がオンラインで{公開|こうかい}された。
examples.english: The game record of the Meijin title match has been published online.

notes:
Compound of {棋|き} ('board game', especially shogi, go, and chess) and {譜|ふ} ('record; score; notation' — the same character used in {楽譜|がくふ}, 'sheet music'). Both elements are literary kanji rarely used outside such compounds.

USAGE:
- A specialized but standard term among shogi and go players; almost every serious player reads {棋譜|きふ}.
- The verbs used with {棋譜|きふ} reflect how records are handled:
  - {棋譜|きふ}を{取|と}る: to record the moves as a game is played.
  - {棋譜|きふ}を{並|なら}べる: to reproduce/play through a recorded game on a board.
  - {棋譜|きふ}を{残|のこ}す: to leave a game record (for posterity).
- Note the homophone {寄付|きふ} ('donation') — context and kanji distinguish them.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {棋譜|きふ}を{取|と}る: to record a game
- {棋譜|きふ}を{並|なら}べる: to play through a game record
- {棋譜|きふ}を{残|のこ}す: to leave a record of the game
- プロの{棋譜|きふ}: professional game records
- {棋譜|きふ}{解析|かいせき}: game record analysis

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {楽譜|がくふ}: sheet music — uses the same {譜|ふ} element; 'score' in the musical sense.
- {譜面|ふめん}: score; notation — general term for written records of music; shares the 'notation' sense.
- {記録|きろく}: record — generic word for any record; {棋譜|きふ} is a specific kind of {記録|きろく}.
- {寄付|きふ}: donation — a homophone with different kanji; easy to confuse in speech.
